original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Price one complete changed itinerary with both paid and productive histograms. Check #5693/#5698 for overlap and their exact hypotheses before another coframe search. Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Open item 3 of research/char2-jets (PR #2162): whether the Lemma F flow obstructs characteristic-2 jets at every order on the three no-wild configurations jf0, jf1, jf2. Integer (Z-valued, coefficient +-1) lifts of the four first-order flows are found and checked, and a valuation lemma turns them into an all-order obstruction for exact-support, unit-coordinate deformations.
scope_change_reason: The card's quantified-proposition variation: one decoder-rank question left explicitly open by a merged package. It is a rank-3 decoder lower-bound mechanism (the T = 3 pairing-cost problem), not a supplier change, so no invoice is priced.
bottleneck_link: Side result. It settles which valuation certificates can prove the T = 3 decoder floor cost >= v on the predecessor's hard instances: uniform-order jets cannot, so any valuation route must use non-uniform incidence orders. It does not change kappa.
stop_rule: Stop at the first configuration line without a 2-local integer lift, or once all four immovable lines carry a checked certificate; do not extend to (A) or other configurations in this package.
evidence: verify.py (standard library, about 0.2 s): recomputes incidences, harmonic lines and first-order immovability from the pinned jf0..2 inputs (immovable exactly jf0 {0}, jf1 {7}, jf2 {0,2}); finds each lift by elimination over Z_(2) and requires +-1 coefficients equal to CERTIFICATE.json; checks the exponent identity exactly; controls: 200 random rational points per line, the Q sign parity, 200 random unit jets over F2[[eps]]/(eps^24) with nu(N_h) >= min nu(N_e) (attained 96-112 times per line), and 16 single-edge mutations per line all rejected. The valuation theorem is a written proof in README.md, without a proof-kernel check.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does a non-uniform VCR2 certificate (incidence valuations not all above the immovable diagonal, or non-unit coordinates) exist for jf0, jf1 or jf2?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the remaining B-independent valuation route to cost >= v on these instances; uniform-order jets are now excluded.
open_questions.first_step: Set up a linear program over valuation vectors on the full pattern's directed cycles, with the diagonal of each immovable line bounded by the minimum over its certificate edges.
open_questions.blocked_by: The directed-cycle condition ranges over all cycles, and dropping unit coordinates leaves the scope of the identity's corollary.

open_questions.question: Which minimisers of jf1 and jf2 contain the edge set of a certificate in supp B?
open_questions.why_it_matters: For those B the B-dependent jet test also fails at every order; the count may account for the six jf1 minimisers that pass neither predecessor test.
open_questions.first_step: Regenerate the minimisers with research/char2-jets c/enumall and intersect their supports with the four edge sets in CERTIFICATE.json.
open_questions.blocked_by: The minimiser lists are regenerated by a C enumerator rather than stored.

open_questions.question: Does every first-order immovable harmonic line of a no-wild configuration admit an integer lift with an odd harmonic coefficient?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A line whose F2 flow has no Z_(2) lift is the only place a higher-order jet could survive.
open_questions.first_step: Run local_solve from verify.py on the 25 non-rigid immovable atoms of PR #2351 (research/pool121-jet-rigidity), where orders >= 3 remain untested.
